study type: secondary analysis of retrospective cohort studies
outcome: incidence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
cohort: 74 pregnancies in 61 patients with a history of open cardiac surgery compared with 219 pregnancies in healthy controls
finding: Patients with a history of cardiac surgery were not more likely to experience hypertensive disorders during pregnancy or deliver low-birthweight neonates but had a higher likelihood of operative delivery, although not specifically cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Patients with a history of cardiac surgery were more likely to have an operative delivery but there was no difference in cesarean delivery rates compared with healthy controls.
birth_weight: neonates born to patients with a history of cardiac surgery: 2655±808 g, neonates born to healthy controls: 2844±830 g
